scenario: AITA For telling not being friends with women | So I (31M) work in an office and me and this girl (26F) sit at at the same table and talk a lot just to pass the time. Recently she has started asking me to go out for drinks on Friday after work (as friends not a date). I made excuses why I could not for a couple of weeks, but then she asked me if I disliked her, I thought I would just tell her the truth that I do not do friendships with women. I do not recall what I said verbatim however the gist of it is that, if I spend prolonged time with a woman I start feeling for a lack of a better word 'territorial'. If they start talking with other guys or get attention from them I my intestines start roiling and I feel an extreme sense of agitation (I never act on it and I put on a happy face and persevere) however I hate said feeling and prefer to avoid it and hence I do not do friendships with women. She then said I should see a psychologist (I will not, even though I am flawed, my flaws make up a part of who I am and I do not wish to change), and since then for the past couple of weeks our talking has just been work related. I thought it would be best to be honest however I am thinking maybe I should have made up some excuse. AITA? Addendum I do get same feelings at work however I do not think about work at home and its work so I have no choice but to tolerate them. However I do not wish to put myself through unnecessary discomfort willingly outside of work. I do not wish to feel this way, I know it is not correct, again I never act on it, but I can not help feeling it. I had told this story to a guy I know and he said I must have been be controlling with my previous girlfriends. So just in case people here will make that assumption, it could not be further from the truth. If the lady is already mine I do not mind her talking to or being around other guys, I think because I know she is mine it makes me happy thinking other men might want what I have and can not have it.

Hmm, that's a pretty sensitive topic. Let me break it down. First, I need to understand his perspective. He says he feels territorial and gets agitated when women he's friends with talk to or get attention from other guys. He mentions that he doesn't act on these feelings and just endures them, but he prefers to avoid such situations. He also clarifies that in a relationship, he's okay with his partner interacting with others because he knows she's his. So, it seems like his issue is more about potential romantic feelings or possessiveness in a friendship context. Now, is it right or wrong for him to be honest about this? On one hand, honesty is usually valued in relationships, whether they're friendships or romantic. Being upfront about your feelings can prevent misunderstandings and hurt feelings down the line. On the other hand, telling someone you don't want to be friends because of these feelings might come off as controlling or insecure, which could damage the relationship or make the other person uncomfortable. I also need to consider the impact on the woman. She initiated the idea of going out for drinks as friends, and when he declined and explained his reasons, she suggested he see a psychologist. That indicates she might feel uncomfortable or even threatened by his honesty. It's possible she felt judged or misunderstood, especially if she values her independence and social interactions with others. Another angle is the societal norms around friendships between genders. There's a lot of pressure on men to be emotionally available and not to display possessiveness, even in platonic friendships. His feelings might stem from societal expectations or personal insecurities. It's important to recognize that everyone has different comfort levels, and it's okay to set boundaries, but the way those boundaries are communicated matters a lot. I also wonder about his past relationships. He mentioned that a friend thinks he might have been controlling with previous girlfriends. If that's the case, it could indicate a pattern of behavior that's not healthy, even if he doesn't act on his possessive feelings. It's worth reflecting on whether these feelings are a sign of deeper issues that might affect his current and future relationships. In terms of whether he's "AITA" (Acting Inappropriately Towards A Woman), it's a bit nuanced. Being honest about his feelings is one thing, but the way he expressed it could be seen as dismissive or judgmental of her social behavior. It's possible that he could have handled the situation more tactfully, perhaps by setting boundaries without sharing the underlying reasons, or by finding a compromise that respects both their comfort levels. Overall, while honesty is important, the manner in which it's delivered and the impact it has on the other person are crucial. It might have been better for him to find a way to decline her invitations without sharing such personal and potentially off-putting reasons. That way, he maintains his boundaries without making her feel judged or uncomfortable.
